citation: "The First Presbyterian Church. Indiana Avenue and Twenty-First Street (1887)." Halftone plate facing p. 82 in Philo Adams Otis, The First Presbyterian Church, 1833-1913: A History of the Oldest Organization in Chicago (Chicago: Fleming H. Revell, 1913).
author: Philo Adams Otis (compiler); photographer not named
describes_date: 1887 (the photograph, as its caption dates it); the church as finished about 1872-1873
repository: Internet Archive, item firstpreschurch00otis (scanned from a library copy; also mirrored on Wikimedia Commons as the PDF cited by first_presbyterian_chicago_1833_1913).
locator: Scan leaf n130 (PDF page 131), the plate captioned '(1887)' among the illustrations listed for 'First Presbyterian Church - Indiana Avenue and Twenty-First Street' (pp. 62, 76, 82, 178, 282). The whole plate: the church's west front to Indiana Avenue and its south-west tower and spire, from East 21st Street west of the avenue, 21st Street receding east past the tower.
rights_note: A photograph published in a book in the United States in 1913, in the public domain. Read for forms, counts and proportions; no texture or mesh is derived from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-24 from the Internet Archive's page image https://archive.org/download/firstpreschurch00otis/page/n130.jpg (2247 x 3630 px, sha256 d00519bcced0df8d41e2517713a4a54573f71d554f51ab3167038206df8c4f64); the plate inside its printed border (page px 173-1923 x 450-3026) is committed, scaled to 1050 x 1546 px and greyscale, as data/sources/assets/first_presbyterian_2029_otis_t3066/otis_1913_plate_1887.jpg (T-3066). The book's text (pp. 52-56, 249-250, 291-292) is read from the item's own OCR (firstpreschurch00otis_djvu.txt).
note: The book dates the building and its use: Calvary Presbyterian Church bought the north-east corner of Indiana Avenue and 21st Street (98 ft on the avenue, 178 ft on 21st Street) on 6 June 1870 and pulled down Trinity Church's stone building on it; J. C. Cochrane was the architect, the corner stone was laid in November 1870, and on 8 October 1871 the west, north and south walls stood with the roof trusses in place (pp. 52-53). Calvary united with the First Church in October 1871 and the united First Presbyterian Church finished the building to Calvary's plans (p. 56); the spire was framed on the vacant lot across the avenue and raised piece by piece (pp. 249-250). The final service in it was held on Sunday 29 December 1912, before the congregation moved to 41st Street (pp. 291-292). The plate is a level view camera's photograph: the tower's and the front's verticals stand vertical, 21st Street's kerbs and roadway meet at about (890, 1450) px of the committed copy, and the west front's horizontals run level, so the camera looked due east down 21st Street, square to the front, with a long lens: the front reads 18.7 px/m from the gable's north foot to the tower's south corner, and the spire's axis stands over the tower face's centre. It shows the brick west front under one steep gable with a coped verge on corbels and a cross at its apex, a round window in the gable, a traceried rose over three lancets, a lancet each side lower down, a gabled stone porch at the centre with a pointed doorway; a low narrow bay at the front's north end; and the square brick tower at the south-west corner in three stages between angle buttresses (a pointed door at its foot, a traceried two-light window with a rose above in the second stage, a louvred belfry with a rose head in the third), gablets and corner pinnacles at its head, and a tall slated octagonal spire with a band of lucarnes about half-way up and a finial.
